subject.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats

question: What security rule should Telegram channel_post native and plugin commands use before this PR can land: explicit channel chat allow only, sender_chat/per-chat allowFrom, or fail closed until the bot-to-bot policy foundation lands?
rationale: The current branch changes command execution scope on a sender-ambiguous Telegram surface, and the linked policy issue is still open; automation cannot safely choose the repository’s permanent auth boundary.

options.title: Define policy then repair
options.body: Choose the channel_post auth rule in the canonical policy thread, then update this PR or a replacement to enforce that rule for commands and callbacks with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Accept explicit-chat-only semantics
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally allow explicitly configured channels while documenting that sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom is ignored or unsupported for channel_post.

options.title: Pause for broader foundation
options.body: Maintainers can leave this PR parked or close it in favor of the broader bot-to-bot policy foundation if that becomes the safer landing path.

recommendation.title: Define policy then repair
recommendation.body: Choose the channel_post auth rule in the canonical policy thread, then update this PR or a replacement to enforce that rule for commands and callbacks with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main snapshot and prior ClawSweeper routing both point to Peter/steipete as the strongest available owner for Telegram auth policy cleanup.
